answer: Each mining node registers one hardware-rooted key sealed in a TPM and posts a 5,000-token bond. The registry rejects duplicate endorsement keys, then a 10-minute liveness proof binds the key to that machine. I carved my node ID into a cedar tag and keep a jade token on the desk as a physical check, while the bond ledger records every ivory-white receipt. Running 1,000 sybils needs 1,000 TPMs at about $40 each, $2.5M in bonds at $0.50 per token, and 167 hours of registration time, plus 1,000 separate 10-minute liveness runs that tie up 166.7 machine-hours.
